# REQ-2283: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2283

#### Bug description

Both `MessagePackGenerator` (CS8785) and `MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer` (AD0001) throw `IndexOutOfRangeException` when a `[MessagePackObject]` type has a member whose type is a **closed generic value type defined in a referenced assembly**.

Because the generator then "will not contribute to the output", the compiling assembly silently ends up with **no generated resolver at all**. It is only a warning, so a normal build looks fine, but trimmed and NativeAOT apps fail at runtime. In our case three assemblies of a large app had been shipping without a resolver across two releases before we noticed.

#### Repro steps

Two projects. `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack;
namespace Lib;

[MessagePackObject]
public partial record struct Item<T>([property: Key(0)] string Key);
```

`app`, with a `ProjectReference` to `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack; using Lib;
namespace App;

[MessagePackObject]
public sealed partial record Cmd([property: Key(0)] string Scope)
{
    [Key(1)] public Item<int> Member { get; init; }
}
```

Then `dotnet build` on `app`. Both projects are in the attached `mp-repro.zip`.

#### Expected behavior

A clean build, with a generated resolver in `app`.
#### Actual behavior

```
CSC : warning CS8785: Generator 'MessagePackGenerator' failed to generate source. It will not
contribute to the output and compilation errors may occur as a result. Exception was of type
'IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the bounds of the array.'.
CSC : warning AD0001: Analyzer 'MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Analyzers.MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer'
threw an exception of type 'System.IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the
bounds of the array.'.
```

`app.dll` contains no `GeneratedMessagePackResolver`.

- Version used: MessagePack 3.1.8
- Runtime: .NET 10 (SDK 10.0.204), Windows 11

#### Additional context

**What triggers it.** `Item` is declared in `lib`, `Cmd` in `app`:

| `Item` declared as | result |
|---|---|
| `record struct Item<T>` | **crash** |
| `struct Item<T>` | **crash** |
| `struct Item` | ok |
| `record struct Item` | ok |
| `class Item<T>` | ok |
| `record class Item<T>` | ok |

So it needs all three of: **generic**, **value type**, **from a referenced assembly**. Moving the identical `Item<T>` declaration into `app` itself makes the crash disappear, which is what makes this specific to metadata symbols.
**Stack trace.**

```
System.IndexOutOfRangeException: Index was outside the bounds of the array.
   at TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo(INamedTypeSymbol formattedType, ISymbol callerSymbol)
   at TypeCollector.CollectGeneric(INamedTypeSymbol type, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 661
   at TypeCollector.CollectCore(ITypeSymbol typeSymbol, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 371
   at TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo(INamedTypeSymbol formattedType, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 1062
   at TypeCollector.CollectCore(ITypeSymbol typeSymbol, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 386
   at TypeCollector.Collect() in TypeCollector.cs:line 300
   at MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.AnalyzeSymbol(SymbolAnalysisContext, ReferenceSymbols, AnalyzerOptions) in MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.cs:line 431
```

`CollectGeneric` line 661 is the closed-generic branch that calls `GetObjectInfo` directly:

```csharp
else
{
    // NOTE: ... closed generic types such as `Foo<string>` are not registered as a formatter.
    this.GetObjectInfo(type, callerSymbol);
```

so `GetObjectInfo` runs against a type that has no syntax. Several diagnostic paths inside it index `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` directly (lines 735, 1009, 1101) instead of using `FirstOrDefault()` the way the neighbouring `GetIdentifierLocation` / `GetLocation` / `GetParameterListLocation` helpers already do, and that collection is empty for a metadata symbol. I did not narrow down which of the three fires.

**Getting the stack trace.** Console output truncates the exception to its message; `-p:ErrorLog=out.sarif` preserves the full description, including the stack trace and an `ISymbol:` context line naming the offending type:

```
dotnet build -p:ErrorLog=out.sarif
```

**Workaround.** Putting `[MessagePackFormatter(typeof(ItemFormatter<>))]` on the generic value type short-circuits `CollectCore` (line 356) before `GetObjectInfo` is reached, at the cost of hand-writing the formatter.

**Possibly related:** #2092 reports CS8785 from the v3 generator, but with a different inner exception and no repro.

story.summary: Stops the generator and analyzer from crashing on a closed generic struct (or record struct) that comes from a referenced assembly. Two diagnostic sites in TypeCollector no longer read `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]`; they use a null-safe lookup instead. Every diagnostic the TypeCollector reports now passes through a new filter that drops it unless its location is a source tree in the current compilation. Three new tests compile a defining assembly to a metadata-only image, then check that the consuming project builds with no diagnostics and gets a resolver. The change also turns off `EnforceCodeStyleInBuild` for the whole repo and adds README and MsgPack004 doc text.
story.why: The issue reports IndexOutOfRangeException (CS8785/AD0001) because diagnostic paths index an empty `DeclaringSyntaxReferences` on metadata symbols. The generator then emits no resolver at all.
touches_beyond_requirement: Directory.Build.props sets EnforceCodeStyleInBuild from true to false for every project in the repo. This has nothing to do with the bug.

The new filter drops every TypeCollector diagnostic whose location is not in this compilation's source, including Location.None ones. The fix only needed to avoid the crash; this changes when existing rules fire.
README.md and doc/analyzers/MsgPack004.md gain new sections describing the new suppression behaviour.
story.confidence_overview: High that the two edited sites no longer index past an empty array. Medium that the tests reproduce the original crash: they mirror the issue's repro, but I cannot see that they fail without the fix. The issue names three crash sites (old lines 735, 1009, 1101). Only two edits are visible, so the third (old ~735) may still index [0]. Low-to-medium comfort with the broad suppression filter and the build-props change.

claims.text: The BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull diagnostic now uses GetPropertyIdentifierLocation, which returns null rather than throwing. Null comes back when there is no syntax, and also when the syntax is not a PropertyDeclarationSyntax (soft `as` cast replaces the old hard cast).
claims.requirement_quote: Several diagnostic paths inside it index `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` directly (lines 735, 1009, 1101) instead of using `FirstOrDefault()`

claims.text: The added usings (Microsoft.CodeAnalysis, Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Testing) only supply MetadataReference, Compilation, ReferenceAssemblies and TestBehaviors for the new test helpers.
Directory.Build.props turns off EnforceCodeStyleInBuild repo-wide. The bug fix does not need this, and it removes a build-time quality gate for all projects.
README adds a section stating that closed generic types from referenced assemblies are supported and that their member diagnostics are reported only by the defining assembly.
MsgPack004.md adds a section stating that the analyzer only reports members declared in the current project.

The TypeCollector constructor wraps the analyzer's report callback so every diagnostic goes through ReportIfLocatedInCompilation. When no callback is given (generator path), reportDiagnostic stays null.

ReportIfLocatedInCompilation forwards a diagnostic only if its Location is in source and that SourceTree belongs to the current compilation. Diagnostics with Location.None (null location) are silently dropped.
claims.requirement_quote: so `GetObjectInfo` runs against a type that has no syntax

claims.text: The MemberNeedsKey diagnostic now gets its location via `DeclaringSyntaxReferences.FirstOrDefault()?`, so a metadata member with no syntax yields a null location instead of throwing IndexOutOfRangeException.
claims.requirement_quote: Several diagnostic paths inside it index `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` directly (lines 735, 1009, 1101) instead of using `FirstOrDefault()`

claims.text: Test ClosedGenericStruct_FromMetadataReference uses a generic struct with a keyed member, defined in a metadata-only assembly, as a member type. It expects no diagnostics and a generated `TempProject.MyResolver.g.cs`.
claims.requirement_quote: So it needs all three of: **generic**, **value type**, **from a referenced assembly**.

claims.text: Test ClosedGenericRecordStruct_FromMetadataReference reproduces the issue's exact Lib/App repro (record struct Item<T>, record Cmd with an `Item<int>` member) at LanguageVersion.Latest. It expects no diagnostics and a generated `App.AppResolver.g.cs`.
claims.requirement_quote: A clean build, with a generated resolver in `app`.

claims.text: Test ClosedGenericStruct_FromMetadataReference_UnkeyedMember uses a metadata generic struct with an unattributed public member. It asserts that the consuming project reports nothing, which pins the decision to drop MsgPack004 for metadata members.
claims.requirement_quote: Moving the identical `Item<T>` declaration into `app` itself makes the crash disappear, which is what makes this specific to metadata symbols.

claims.text: RunWithMetadataReferenceAsync really tests the requirement in two steps. First, VerifyCS with no expected diagnostics fails on any AD0001/CS8785. Second, it runs the generator directly and asserts there are no warning-or-higher diagnostics and that the expected resolver hint name is among the generated sources.

CompileToMetadataReferenceAsync and CreateCompilation emit the defining source to a PE image and reference it via MetadataReference.CreateFromImage. Its symbols therefore have no DeclaringSyntaxReferences, which is the trigger condition.

refusals.why: A change beyond the requirement that weakens build checks, likely made so the new code compiles without fixing style violations.

refusals.what: Global diagnostic filter that drops any TypeCollector diagnostic not located in this compilation's source, including Location.None.
refusals.why: Goes beyond fixing the crash. It changes when existing analyzer rules surface to users, and the docs advertise this as policy; a human should decide that policy.

findings.description: EnforceCodeStyleInBuild is switched off for the whole repository. This looks like it was done to get past style errors in the new code rather than fixing them, and it silently weakens build checks everywhere.

The filter drops every diagnostic with Location.None, not just metadata ones. Analyzers are allowed to report Location.None diagnostics; only out-of-compilation source locations are forbidden, so the remark at 1440-1442 overstates this. Any existing source-type diagnostic whose location helper returns null (e.g. GetIdentifierLocation or GetParameterListLocation when syntax has an unexpected shape) is now silently suppressed instead of reported.

The hard cast became a soft `as PropertyDeclarationSyntax`. For a source positional record property, the declaring syntax is a ParameterSyntax, so the location becomes null and the BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull diagnostic is now dropped by the filter rather than reported. No test covers this path.

The issue lists three `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` sites (old lines 735, 1009, 1101). Only two are visibly changed. The one at old ~735 is not in the diff; if it still indexes [0], a metadata generic struct reaching that path can still crash. Owner should confirm that site.

New documentation section describing the support and diagnostic-suppression policy for referenced-assembly generic types.
New documentation section stating that MsgPack004 does not report members of referenced-assembly types.
